question: Spot the **correct spelling** of early film base compound.
solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The correct spelling is 'Nitrocellulose'.**

__
 
• **Nitrocellulose** is a compound used as an early film base and is also known as cellulose nitrate.
 
• It is highly flammable and was once widely used in photography and filmmaking.
 
• Over time, it was replaced by safer materials due to its tendency to degrade and pose fire hazards.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Nitrocellulose'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Interesting facts about Nitrocellulose:**

 
• Nitrocellulose was initially used in the production of gunpowder and explosives before its application in film production.
 
• It is known for its glossy finish and is still used in some musical instrument coatings.
 
• The instability of nitrocellulose led to the development of safer, more durable alternatives for films.
